curate-combinations tops up any plant under the 5-companion cap from the whole-catalog roster, so it legitimately pairs two older plants (§19, §25 step 3). All four endpoints here are round-7 plants that were below the cap and now sit at exactly 5.

draft-hardiness targets hardiness_rating IS NULL, so it backfilled round 7's 76 plants, never drafted since July 15. Remediation of a genuinely skipped step rather than a stray write, and the reason round-status.ts now exists (§25).

the 20 rows round 8's full-catalog regeneration rewrote, since validated against WCVP by cross-check-native-region.ts: 13 were already correct and 7 were corrected on July 28. The regeneration overreach itself is fixed upstream, where --round or --all is now required (§26).

the July 28 style re-tag pass (scripts/curate-styles.ts), which judged all 595 plants against the tightened definitions in lib/style-tags.ts and is recorded in docs/database-log.md. Catalog-wide by design and nothing to do with round 8 — it simply lands inside a baseline-to-now window because it ran after the round. It cannot be excluded by cleared_at either: the style pass finished 13:06 on July 28 and round 8's own greenery and image remediation ran at 15:20 and 15:30, so any window wide enough to hold round 8's real work also holds this.

cleared_why: Round 8 is finished. The last three plants with no hero at all (Crown imperial, Golden chain tree, Lavender mist meadow rue) were sourced from Wikimedia on 2026-07-29, picked, verified to high and signed off, taking the round to 97 of 101. The four remaining holds are recorded verdicts, not outstanding work: 2 species no available photograph can confirm (American alumroot, Persian ironwood) and the prickly-pear's tag flag, which has no mechanism to record a rejection. Closing the window here so later catalog-wide work stops being reported as this round spilling out of its batch — the failure mode that produced 287 false failures the day after the round was called clean.
